rule_summary: A condition is a pre-existing disease (PED) only if it was diagnosed by a physician, or medical advice/treatment was recommended or received, within 36 months before the policy commencement date. Conditions first diagnosed after the policy started, or only more than 36 months before it, do not meet this definition.
verbatim_quote: "Pre-existing disease (PED)" means any condition, ailment, injury or disease: a) that is/are diagnosed by a physician not more than 36 months prior to the date of commencement of the policy issued by the insurer; or b) for which medical advice or treatment was recommended by, or received from, a physician, not more than 36 months prior to the date of commencement of the policy.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 1.6 (definition of Pre-existing disease)
use_when: Insurer rejects or deducts a claim calling the condition 'pre-existing' although the first diagnosis/advice/treatment was after policy commencement or more than 36 months before it. Check that the policy is on a product compliant with the 2024 Regulations (existing products had to be aligned by 30.09.2024).

rule_summary: The waiting period for disclosed pre-existing diseases cannot exceed 36 months of continuous coverage.
verbatim_quote: Waiting period for pre-existing diseases disclosed by the persons to be insured, shall be maximum up to 36 months of continuous coverage under the Health Insurance policy.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 7 (Pre-existing diseases and specific waiting period)
use_when: Claim for a disclosed PED is rejected after 36+ months of continuous cover (including ported/migrated credit), or the policy wording still applies a longer (e.g. 48-month) PED waiting period.

rule_summary: A specific-disease/treatment waiting period can be at most 36 months from policy commencement, does not apply to treatment needed due to an accident, and the disease/treatment must be covered once the period is completed with continuous renewal.
verbatim_quote: "Specific waiting period" means a period up to 36 months from the commencement of a health insurance policy during which period specified diseases/treatments (except due to an accident) are not covered. On completion of the period, diseases/treatments shall be covered provided the policy has been continuously renewed without any break.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 1.7 (definition of Specific waiting period)
use_when: Rejection citing a specific-disease waiting period (e.g. cataract, hernia, joint replacement) after 36 months of continuous cover, or where the treatment was necessitated by an accident.

rule_summary: After 60 continuous months of health cover (portability and migration periods count), the insurer cannot contest the policy or any claim on grounds of non-disclosure or misrepresentation, except for established fraud.
verbatim_quote: After completion of sixty continuous months of coverage (including portability and migration) in health insurance policy, no policy and claim shall be contestable by the insurer on grounds of non-disclosure, misrepresentation, except on grounds of established fraud. This period of sixty continuous months is called as moratorium period.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 8 (Moratorium)
use_when: Insurer rejects a claim or cancels the policy for non-disclosure/misrepresentation (e.g. undisclosed PED) after 5+ years of continuous cover, without proving fraud. Applies to policies of general and health insurers.

rule_summary: The 5-year moratorium runs on the sum insured of the first policy; for any later increase in sum insured, a fresh 5 years applies only to the enhanced portion.
verbatim_quote: The moratorium would be applicable for the sums insured of the first policy and subsequently completion of Five continuous years would be applicable from date of enhancement of sums insured only on the enhanced limits.
source_title: Annexures to Master Circular on Health Insurance Business dated 29.05.2024
clause_ref: Annexure-1 (Customer Information Sheet), row 12 'Things to remember' - Moratorium Period
use_when: Insurer uses non-disclosure to deny the whole claim after 5 years where only the sum insured was enhanced recently: the original sum insured remains protected by the moratorium; only the enhanced amount can still be contested.

rule_summary: Even after the moratorium, the policy is non-contestable except for proven fraud, but permanent exclusions written in the policy contract still apply.
verbatim_quote: After the expiry of Moratorium Period no health insurance policy shall be contestable except for proven fraud and permanent exclusions specified in the policy contract.
source_title: Annexures to Master Circular on Health Insurance Business dated 29.05.2024
clause_ref: Annexure-1 (Customer Information Sheet), row 12 'Things to remember' - Moratorium Period
use_when: Assessing whether the moratorium defeats a rejection: it defeats non-disclosure/misrepresentation grounds, but not a genuine permanent exclusion in the policy wording.

rule_summary: If the policy is renewed within the grace period (15 days for monthly premium, 30 days otherwise), all accrued credits - sum insured, no claim bonus, specific and PED waiting periods, moratorium - remain protected.
verbatim_quote: If the policy is renewed during grace period, all the credits (sum insured, No Claim Bonus, Specific Waiting periods, waiting periods for pre-existing diseases, Moratorium period etc.) accrued under the policy shall be protected. The same is applicable for both Indemnity and Benefit products.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 8(b) (Grace Period for payment of premium)
use_when: Insurer treats a renewal paid within the grace period as a 'break in policy' and restarts waiting periods or the moratorium count.

rule_summary: When moving to another policy with the same insurer, accrued credits (sum insured, NCB, specific and PED waiting periods, moratorium) carry over to the migrated policy.
verbatim_quote: In case of migration of one policy to another with the same Insurer, the policyholder (including all members under family cover and group insurance policies) can transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, Specific Waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing diseases, Moratorium period etc. in the previous policy to the migrated policy.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 11 (Migration in case of Indemnity policies)
use_when: Claim rejected for waiting period/PED/non-disclosure after the policyholder migrated plans within the same insurer and the insurer ignored time served under the earlier policy.

rule_summary: On porting to a new insurer, credits for sum insured, NCB, specific waiting periods, PED waiting period and moratorium transfer from the existing insurer to the acquiring insurer.
verbatim_quote: By porting, the policyholder is entitled to transfer the credits gained to the extent of the Sum Insured, No Claim Bonus, specific waiting periods, waiting period for pre-existing disease, Moratorium period etc. from the Existing Insurer to the Acquiring Insurer in the previous policy.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VII(3)(ii) (Portability in case of Health Indemnity Policies)
use_when: Acquiring insurer rejects a claim for PED/specific waiting period or non-disclosure by counting only time since port-in and ignoring continuous cover with the previous insurer (to the extent of the previous sum insured).

rule_summary: A health policy's renewal cannot be refused because claims were made in earlier years (except benefit policies that terminate on payout, such as critical illness).
verbatim_quote: An insurer shall not deny the renewal of a health insurance policy on the ground that the insured had made a claim or claims in the preceding policy years, except for benefit based policies where the policy terminates following payment of the benefit covered under the policy like critical illness policy.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 9.2 (Renewal of health policies)
use_when: Insurer refuses renewal (or threatens non-renewal) after the policyholder made or disputed a claim.

rule_summary: Each insurer must have a Board-approved AYUSH coverage policy that addresses placing AYUSH treatment at par with other treatments so policyholders can choose their treatment.
verbatim_quote: Insurers shall have a Board approved policy for providing AYUSH coverage, which interalia, shall include their approach towards placing AYUSH treatments at par with other treatments for the purpose of health insurance so as to provide an option for the policyholders to choose treatment of their choice.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 5 (AYUSH coverage)
use_when: AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, Homeopathy) hospitalisation claim is rejected or capped far below allopathic equivalents; check the policy wording's AYUSH clause and ask for the insurer's AYUSH policy. Coverage still depends on the specific policy.

rule_summary: Insurers are to endeavour to cover modern/advanced treatments such as robotic surgery, oral chemotherapy, immunotherapy injections, intravitreal injections, stereotactic radiosurgery, deep brain stimulation, balloon sinuplasty, IONM and stem-cell therapy for haematological conditions. This is an 'endeavour' obligation; actual cover and sub-limits depend on the policy wording.
verbatim_quote: Insurers shall endeavour to cover Technological Advancements and Treatments in their products. Examples of prevalent treatment / procedures that need to be included, and not limited to the following:
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 2 (Technological Advancements & Treatments)
use_when: Claim for a modern treatment (e.g. robotic surgery, oral chemo, immunotherapy, intravitreal injection) is rejected as 'not covered/experimental'; supports the argument together with the policy's own modern-treatment clause.

rule_summary: Every insurer must run a separate channel for health claims and grievances of senior citizens and publish its details on its website.
verbatim_quote: All insurers shall establish a separate channel to address the health insurance related claims and grievances of senior citizens. The details of such channel shall be available in the website of the insurers.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Insurance Products) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Schedule III, clause 11 (Special provisions for senior citizens)
use_when: Claimant is a senior citizen - direct the claim follow-up/grievance to the insurer's dedicated senior-citizen channel and cite this if none is available.

rule_summary: The insurer must decide a cashless authorisation request immediately and within one hour of receiving it (systems were to be in place by 31 July 2024).
verbatim_quote: Insurer shall decide on the request for cashless authorization immediately but not more than one hour of receipt of request.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 15(b) (Approval for Cashless facility)
use_when: Cashless pre-authorisation left pending for hours, forcing the patient to pay a deposit or convert to reimbursement.

rule_summary: Final cashless authorisation at discharge must be granted within 3 hours of the hospital's request, and the patient must not be made to wait for discharge.
verbatim_quote: Insurer shall grant final authorization within three hours of the receipt of discharge authorization request from the hospital. In no case, the policyholder shall be made to wait to be discharged from the Hospital.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 16(a) (Final authorization for Discharge)
use_when: Patient held back at discharge while the insurer/TPA delays final bill approval.

rule_summary: If final authorisation is delayed beyond 3 hours, any additional amount the hospital charges (e.g. extra room-day charges) must be borne by the insurer from its shareholders' funds, not deducted from the policyholder.
verbatim_quote: If there is any delay beyond three hours, the additional amount if any charged by the hospital shall be borne by the insurer from shareholder's fund.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 16(b) (Final authorization for Discharge)
use_when: Bill includes an extra day's room/nursing charges because discharge approval took more than 3 hours, and the insurer deducts or passes it to the patient.

rule_summary: If the policyholder dies during treatment, the insurer must immediately process the claim and get the body released from the hospital immediately.
verbatim_quote: In the event of the death of the policyholder during the treatment, the insurer shall: i. immediately process the request for claim settlement. ii. get the mortal remains (dead body) released from the hospital immediately
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 16(c) (Final authorization for Discharge)
use_when: Hospital withholds the body pending insurer approval of the final bill.

rule_summary: For group health policies, the insurer must obtain member details from the master policyholder so cashless works from day one, and no claim can be denied because member details were not available.
verbatim_quote: In order to provide cashless claim settlement from the date of commencement of cover, the Insurer shall obtain the details of members of the group from the master policyholder, at the earliest. No claim shall be denied for non-availability of details of members of the group.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter II, A.II (General Principles - group policies)
use_when: Employer/group policy claim denied or cashless refused because the employee/dependant 'is not yet in the member list'.

rule_summary: A claim cannot be rejected or closed merely because documents are pending or because the claim was intimated late.
verbatim_quote: No claim shall be rejected or closed for want of documents or for delayed intimation of claim.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(1)(ii) (At the time of claim); also Section 2, Chapter V, para 22
use_when: Insurer/TPA closes or rejects the claim citing 'documents not submitted', 'query not replied' or 'intimation beyond 24/48 hours / 30 days'.

rule_summary: After a claim is intimated, the insurer/TPA must collect the required documents from the hospital; the policyholder is not required to submit them.
verbatim_quote: Pursuant to intimation of the claim, Insurers and Third-Party Administrators (TPAs), shall collect the required documents from the Hospitals. Policyholder shall not be required to submit the documents.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(3) (Settlement of health insurance Claims)
use_when: TPA demands that the patient obtain and submit hospital records (indoor case papers, bills, discharge summary) and delays/denies the claim for their absence.

rule_summary: Insurers must ask for all necessary documents specified in the policy at one go, not in piecemeal queries.
verbatim_quote: Call for all necessary documents as specified in the policy document at one go and avoid calling such documents/information in a piece meal manner;
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 23(4) (Treatment of Policyholders and Claimants)
use_when: Repeated, successive document queries from the insurer/TPA that delay settlement, or demands for documents not listed in the policy document.

rule_summary: The specific documents needed for a claim, and the claim procedure, must be listed in the policy document and on the insurer's website.
verbatim_quote: necessary specific documentation required to support the claim are listed in the policy document along with the procedures to be followed for settlement of claims, in addition to placing the information prominently on their website.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 22(1)(a) (Settlement of Claims)
use_when: Insurer asks for a document that is not in the policy's list of claim documents, or rejects for its absence.

rule_summary: Reimbursement (non-cashless) health claims must be settled within 15 days from submission of the claim.
verbatim_quote: Settlement of claims (other than cashless) shall be settled within fifteen days from submission of claim.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(6); also Schedule A Citizens' Charter (Health), item 4
use_when: Reimbursement claim pending beyond 15 days after submission; combine with R-CLAIM-DELAY-INTEREST for interest on delay.

rule_summary: If a claim is not settled within the specified timelines, the claimant is entitled to interest at bank rate + 2% from the date of claim intimation until payment, payable by the insurer on its own (suo motu).
verbatim_quote: In case the claim is not settled within the specified timelines, then the claimant is entitled for interest at bank rate plus 2 percent from the date of receipt of intimation to till the date of payment. Such interest shall be suo-moto paid by the insurers.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(2)(ii) (Processing of claim)
use_when: Claim paid late (beyond the 15-day reimbursement TAT or other specified timeline) without interest; demand interest in the grievance.

rule_summary: 'Bank Rate' for interest calculations is the RBI bank rate prevailing on 1 April of the financial year in which the claim fell due.
verbatim_quote: "Bank Rate" means Bank rate fixed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) which is prevalent as on 1st day of the financial year in which the claim has fallen due.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 5(3) (Definitions)
use_when: Computing the delay interest (bank rate + 2%) owed on a late claim payment.

rule_summary: Whenever a claim is repudiated, rejected or partly disallowed, the insurer must give full details with reference to the specific terms and conditions of the policy document.
verbatim_quote: In case, the claim is repudiated or rejected or disallowed partially, details shall be communicated to the claimant along with full details giving reference to the specific terms and conditions of the policy document.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(5); see also Health Master Circular Chapter I para 17(b)
use_when: Rejection/deduction letter says only 'not payable', 'as per policy terms', 'non-medical expenses' or 'reasonable and customary' without quoting the specific clause relied upon.

rule_summary: No claim may be repudiated without approval of the insurer's Product Management Committee or its three-member Claims Review Committee (CRC).
verbatim_quote: No claim shall be repudiated without the approval of Product Management Committee (PMC) or a three-member sub-group of PMC called the Claims Review Committee (CRC).
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(3)(iii)(4); see also Health Master Circular Chapter I para 17(a) and Chapter II A.I(4)(b)
use_when: Full rejection issued by a TPA or claims officer; ask the insurer to confirm CRC approval of the repudiation.

rule_summary: All applicable exclusions must be written into the policy document; the insurer cannot make further deductions from a claim in the name of any exclusion not in the policy.
verbatim_quote: Insurers shall mandatorily include in the policy document all the applicable exclusions for a particular product. No further deductions shall be made from the claim amount in the name of any other exclusions.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 2, Chapter IV, para 16.3 (General Principles governing issuance of policies)
use_when: Deductions labelled as 'non-payable', 'non-medical', 'not covered' or similar that cannot be traced to an exclusion or limit actually written in the policy document.

rule_summary: A health policy must clearly state any sub-limits, proportionate deductions and package-rate provisions, with a cross reference to the relevant policy section. (The 2024 framework has no separate rule restricting which items proportionate deduction may apply to; that restriction lived in the superseded 2020 standardisation circular, so rely on the policy wording.)
verbatim_quote: The sub-limits, Proportionate Deductions and the existence of Package rates if any, with cross reference to the concerned policy section,
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Schedule C, para 3.1(ix) (Matters to be stated in a Health Insurance Policy: 'A health insurance policy shall clearly state')
use_when: Insurer applies a proportionate deduction, sub-limit or package-rate cap that is not clearly stated (with section reference) in the policy document; use with R-NO-DEDUCTION-OUTSIDE-LISTED-EXCLUSIONS and then check what the policy wording itself says about proportionate deduction.

rule_summary: The Customer Information Sheet must show financial limits of coverage - sub-limits, co-payment (including any 'Room / ICU charges beyond' limit) and deductibles - that the policyholder will have to bear.
verbatim_quote: In case of a claim, this policy requires you to share the following costs: Expenses exceeding the following Sublimits
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Schedule D, Customer Information Sheet (Health), row 8 'Financial limits of coverage' (template row 'Room / ICU charges beyond ----')
use_when: Room rent/ICU cap or resulting deduction applied although no such limit appears in the CIS/policy schedule; context-dependent because the policy document prevails over the CIS (see R-CIS-POLICY-DOCUMENT-PREVAILS).

rule_summary: If the Customer Information Sheet and the policy document conflict, the policy document's terms prevail.
verbatim_quote: In case of any conflict, the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy document shall prevail.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Schedule D, Customer Information Sheet (Health), Note (ii)
use_when: Caution when a policyholder relies only on the CIS: always verify the limit/exclusion in the full policy wording before challenging.

rule_summary: With several indemnity health policies, the policyholder chooses which policy to claim under; that insurer becomes primary and must coordinate with the other insurers for any balance amount.
verbatim_quote: a) If a policyholder has more than one health insurance policy from different insurers he/she can file for claim settlement as per his/her choice under any policy. b) The Insurer of that chosen policy shall be treated as the primary Insurer.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, V(5)(1) (Claims in respect of multiple Policies - Indemnity)
use_when: Insurer insists the claim be filed first under another policy (e.g. employer group cover) or refuses to coordinate settlement of the balance.

rule_summary: 'Material information' is the important, essential and relevant information and documents explicitly sought by the insurer in the proposal form; disclosure duties apply to both insurer and prospect.
verbatim_quote: "Material Information" for the purpose of these regulations shall mean all important, essential and relevant information and documents explicitly sought by insurer in the proposal form.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 5(10), Explanation (i) (definition of Proposal form / Material Information)
use_when: Insurer alleges non-disclosure of something the proposal form never explicitly asked about (e.g. a minor condition, lifestyle detail or question not in the form).

rule_summary: The insurer must give the insured a copy of the proposal form submitted, along with the policy document, free of charge within 15 days of accepting the proposal.
verbatim_quote: It is the duty of the insurer to furnish to the insured, with no additional charges, either a soft copy or a hard copy of the proposal form submitted by the prospect, along with the policy document within 15 days of the acceptance of a proposal.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 2, Chapter III, para 12.4 (Processing of the proposal Form)
use_when: Non-disclosure rejection: request the proposal form copy to check what was actually asked/declared (and whether it was filled by an agent); non-supply of the copy strengthens the grievance.

rule_summary: Insurers must acknowledge a complaint immediately and resolve it within 14 days, giving reasons with specific reference to policy terms if the complaint is not accepted.
verbatim_quote: On receipt of a complaint, the complainant will have to be given an acknowledgement immediately. Insurers should provide resolution to the complaint within 14 days along with the reasons for not accepting the complaint with specific reference to the relevant terms and conditions of the policy.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(2)(i) (Turnaround time for resolution of complaints); also Schedule A Citizens' Charter (Health), item 6
use_when: Grievance to the insurer's GRO not acknowledged, not resolved within 14 days, or rejected without citing specific policy terms.

rule_summary: A policyholder or beneficiary can complain directly to the insurer and/or its distribution channel (including the TPA) - at a branch, by letter/email, on the insurer's website or via its call centre.
verbatim_quote: Where the policyholder / beneficiary is not satisfied with the services of the insurer or the distribution channel, he / she can lodge complaints directly with the insurer or with the distribution channel including TPA or with both using any one of the following mode:
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(1)(i) (Lodging of complaint)
use_when: Starting escalation: first written complaint to the insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer (and TPA if involved).

rule_summary: Policyholders/claimants can also register a complaint online on IRDAI's Bima Bharosa portal.
verbatim_quote: The policyholder or the claimant also has the option to register the complaint on-line at IRDAI's Bima Bharosa by visiting https://bimabharosa.irdai.gov.in/.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(1) (Lodging of complaint)
use_when: Insurer is not responding, or the policyholder wants the complaint recorded on IRDAI's system and tracked.

rule_summary: Insurers must integrate their grievance portals with Bima Bharosa, with real-time mirroring, so grievances can be registered and tracked online.
verbatim_quote: Insurers shall integrate its grievance portal with the Bima Bharosa portal to facilitate the registering/ tracking of grievance on-line by the policyholders.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(1) (Lodging of complaint)
use_when: Complaint lodged with the insurer does not show up/track on Bima Bharosa, or status is not updated.

rule_summary: Insurers and intermediaries must not prohibit, bar or discourage a policyholder or claimant from complaining to IRDAI.
verbatim_quote: No insurer or distribution channel shall prohibit, bar or discourage any policyholder or claimant from lodging any grievance to the Authority.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 25(3) (Grievance Redressal Procedure)
use_when: Settlement offers or discharge vouchers conditioned on not complaining, or agents/TPA discouraging a complaint.

rule_summary: The insurer's response to any grievance must include contact details of the concerned Insurance Ombudsman for escalation.
verbatim_quote: The response letter of the Insurer in any grievance shall include the contact details of concerned insurance ombudsmen where his/her complaint can be escalated in case, the policyholder is not satisfied by the grievance redressal provided by the Insurer.
source_title: Master Circular on IRDAI (Insurance Products) Regulations 2024 - Health Insurance (Master Circular on Health Insurance Business), Ref IRDAI/HLT/CIR/PRO/84/5/2024
clause_ref: Chapter I, para 19 (Redressal of Grievances of the Policyholder)
use_when: Insurer's grievance reply omits ombudsman details; point this out and escalate.

rule_summary: If the insurer does not resolve the complaint, it must tell the policyholder the options, including the Insurance Ombudsman or Consumer Court, within 14 days from the original date of receipt of the complaint.
verbatim_quote: If complaint is NOT resolved by the Insurer, communicate the details to the Policyholder of options including referring the complainant to Insurance Ombudsman / Consumer Court.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Schedule A, Citizens' Charter (Health), item 6 'Complaints'
use_when: Insurer neither resolves nor informs escalation options within 14 days of the complaint.

rule_summary: A policyholder may approach the Insurance Ombudsman if the complaint is not resolved within 30 days or if the insurer's decision is not acceptable.
verbatim_quote: *(The policyholder may approach the Insurance Ombudsman if his / her complaint is not resolved within 30 days or if the decision of the company is not acceptable to the policyholder.)
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Schedule A, Citizens' Charter (Health), note to item 6 'Complaints'
use_when: Deciding when escalation to the Ombudsman is permitted after a grievance to the insurer.

rule_summary: If not satisfied with the insurer's grievance resolution, unresolved or partially resolved complaints can be escalated to the Insurance Ombudsman of the relevant jurisdiction where the claim amount is up to Rs 50 lakh.
verbatim_quote: In case the complainant is not satisfied with the resolution of grievance provided by the insurer, they can escalate the unresolved / partially resolved complaints to Insurance Ombudsman of concerned jurisdiction, in case the claim amount is up to Rs. 50 lakhs.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(3)(i) (Filing of complaint before Insurance Ombudsman)
use_when: Checking Ombudsman eligibility for a rejected/short-settled claim; above Rs 50 lakh use consumer commission/civil remedies.

rule_summary: An Ombudsman complaint is free of any charge/fee and can be filed in person, online at cioins.co.in, or in writing by post/email.
verbatim_quote: The policyholder has option to take up the matter before insurance ombudsman of competent jurisdiction without any charge / fee through any of the following options: a. In person; b. Online by visiting https://cioins.co.in/Complaint/Online; c. In writing through post or through email by giving complete details.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 1, Part B, VI(3)(ii) (Filing of complaint before Insurance Ombudsman)
use_when: Preparing the Ombudsman complaint; reassure there is no fee and online filing is available.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman handles complaints about delay in claim settlement beyond regulatory timelines and about partial or total repudiation of claims by health insurers.
verbatim_quote: (a) delay in settlement of claims, beyond the time specified in the regulations, framed under the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India Act, 1999; (b) any partial or total repudiation of claims by the life insurer, General insurer or the health insurer;
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 13(1)(a) and (b) (Duties and functions of Insurance Ombudsman)
use_when: Any health claim rejection, partial deduction (short settlement) or delayed settlement.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman can also take up non-observance of IRDAI regulations, circulars, guidelines or the policy terms insofar as they relate to claim delay, repudiation, premium, misrepresentation, policy construction, servicing or issuance issues.
verbatim_quote: any other matter arising from non-observance of or non-adherence to the provisions of any regulations made by the Authority with regard to protection of policyholders interests or otherwise, or of any circular, guideline or instruction issued by the Authority, or of the terms and conditions of the policy contract, insofar as such matter relates to issues referred to in clauses (a) to (h).
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 13(1)(i) (substituted by G.S.R. 147(E) dated 02.03.2021)
use_when: Complaint is based on breach of an IRDAI rule (e.g. cashless/discharge TAT, documents rule, rejection letter not citing a clause).

rule_summary: Before going to the Ombudsman, the complainant must have made a written/email/online representation to the insurer, and either it was rejected, no reply came within one month of the insurer receiving it, or the reply is unsatisfactory.
verbatim_quote: No complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman shall lie unless (a) the complainant 1 [has made a representation in writing or through electronic mail or online through website of the insurer or insurance broker concerned] named in the complaint and-- (i) either the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] had rejected the complaint; or (ii) the complainant had not received any reply within a period of one month after the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] received his representation; or (iii) the complainant is not satisfied with the reply given to him by the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be.]
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 14(3)(a) (as amended by G.S.R. 147(E) dated 02.03.2021)
use_when: Checking whether an Ombudsman complaint is maintainable - ensure a written grievance to the insurer exists (claim rejection letter alone may not be enough; send a representation/grievance first).

rule_summary: The Ombudsman complaint must be filed within one year of the insurer's rejection of the representation, of receiving its unsatisfactory decision, or of expiry of one month from sending the representation if no reply was received.
verbatim_quote: (b) The complaint is made within one year-- (i) after the order of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] rejecting the representation is received; or (ii) after receipt of decision of the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be], which is not to the satisfaction of the complainant; (iii) after expiry of a period of one month from the date of sending the written representation to the insurer 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be,] if the insurer or 1 [ insurance broker, as the case may be], named fails to furnish reply to the complainant.
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 14(3)(b)
use_when: Calculating the deadline to approach the Ombudsman.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman may condone delay in filing (beyond one year) after hearing the insurer's objections and recording reasons.
verbatim_quote: The Ombudsman shall be empowered to condone the delay in such cases as he may consider necessary, after calling for objections of the insurer or insurance broker, as the case may be, against the proposed condonation and after recording reasons for condoning the delay
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 14(4)
use_when: The one-year limit has passed; request condonation with reasons for the delay.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman cannot hear a complaint on the same subject matter that is pending before, or already decided by, a court, consumer forum or arbitrator.
verbatim_quote: No complaint before the Insurance Ombudsman shall be maintainable on the same subject matter on which proceedings are pending before or disposed of by any court or consumer forum or arbitrator.
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 14(5)
use_when: Choosing between Ombudsman and consumer commission - do not file both on the same dispute.

rule_summary: The complaint can be made by the aggrieved person or legal heirs/nominee/assignee to the Ombudsman covering either the insurer's branch/office complained against or the complainant's residence.
verbatim_quote: Any person who has a grievance against an insurer 1 [or insurance broker] may himself or through his legal heirs, nominee or assignee, make a complaint in writing to the Insurance Ombudsman within whose territorial jurisdiction the branch or office of the insurer 1 [or the insurance broker, as the case may be,] complained against or the residential address or place of residence of the complainant is located.
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 14(1) (as amended by G.S.R. 147(E) dated 02.03.2021)
use_when: Selecting which Ombudsman office to file with; nominee/legal heir filing after death of the insured.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman cannot award more than the loss directly suffered, and the award cannot exceed Rs 50 lakh including expenses (raised from Rs 30 lakh on 9 Nov 2023).
verbatim_quote: (i) not award any compensation in excess of the loss suffered by the complainant as a direct consequence of the cause of action; or (ii) not award compensation exceeding rupees 3 [fifty] lakhs (including relevant expenses, if any).
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 17(3), proviso (i)-(ii) ('thirty' substituted by 'fifty' vide Insurance Ombudsman (Amendment) Rules, 2023, G.S.R. 828(E) dated 09.11.2023)
use_when: Deciding whether the Ombudsman is the right forum for the disputed amount.

rule_summary: The Ombudsman should pass the award within three months of receiving all requirements from the complainant.
verbatim_quote: The Ombudsman shall finalise its findings and pass an award within a period of three months of the receipt of all requirements from the complainant.
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 17(4)
use_when: Setting expectations on Ombudsman timelines; follow up if pending beyond 3 months after all documents were submitted.

rule_summary: An Ombudsman award is binding on the insurer.
verbatim_quote: The award of Insurance Ombudsman shall be binding on the insurers 1 [or insurance broker, as the case may be].
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 17(8)
use_when: Insurer ignores or delays paying an award.

rule_summary: The insurer must comply with an Ombudsman award within 30 days of receipt; otherwise it must pay the complainant Rs 5,000 per day as penalty in addition to penal interest - unless the insurer has chosen to appeal.
verbatim_quote: The Insurer is required to comply with the award of the Insurance Ombudsman within 30 days of receipt of award by the Insurer. In case the Insurer does not honour the ombudsman award, a penalty of Rs. 5000/- per day shall be payable to the complainant. Such penalty is in addition to the penal interest liable to be paid by the Insurer under the Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017. This provision will not be applicable in case insurer chooses to appeal against the award of the Insurance Ombudsman.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 2, Chapter VII, para 25.4 (Ombudsman Awards)
use_when: Award in the policyholder's favour not paid within 30 days.

rule_summary: On an Ombudsman award, the insurer must also pay penal interest at bank rate + 2% from the date the claim ought to have been settled.
verbatim_quote: The insurer, in terms of rule 17 (7) of Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017, shall also pay penal interest at a rate, which is 2 percent above bank rate from the date the claim ought to have been settled.
source_title: Master Circular on Protection of Policyholders' Interests, 2024, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/117/9/2024
clause_ref: Section 2, Chapter VII, para 25.2 (Ombudsman Awards)
use_when: Calculating amounts due under an Ombudsman award; include interest in the relief sought.

rule_summary: If the Ombudsman mediates and the complainant accepts the recommendation in writing within 15 days, it is accepted as full and final settlement.
verbatim_quote: If the recommendation of the Ombudsman is acceptable to the complainant, he shall send a communication in writing within fifteen days of receipt of the recommendation, stating clearly that he accepts the settlement as full and final.
source_title: Insurance Ombudsman Rules, 2017 (as amended up to 09.11.2023; CIO consolidated copy)
clause_ref: Rule 16(2) (Complaints settled through mediation)
use_when: Policyholder is offered a mediated settlement - warn that acceptance closes the dispute.

rule_summary: Insurers must file their Self-Contained Note with supporting documents within 7 days of the Ombudsman office's notice (and additional documents within 3 days, in one go).
verbatim_quote: To submit the required SCNs duly supported by the relevant documents within seven (7) days from the date of receipt of the notice from the concerned Office of the Insurance Ombudsman.
source_title: IRDAI Circular: Submission of Self-Contained Note and other related documents to the Office of the Insurance Ombudsmen, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/95/07/2026
clause_ref: Para 3(i)
use_when: Ombudsman hearing delayed because the insurer has not filed its reply/SCN.

rule_summary: If the insurer does not submit the SCN/documents on time, the Ombudsman office will proceed ex parte on the material on record to meet the award timeline.
verbatim_quote: Where an insurer fails to comply with the above, the concerned Office of the Insurance Ombudsman, in order to comply with the timeline provided in Rule 17 (4), shall proceed with the matter, ex parte, without any further delay, basis the material information available on record.
source_title: IRDAI Circular: Submission of Self-Contained Note and other related documents to the Office of the Insurance Ombudsmen, Ref IRDAI/PP&GR/CIR/MISC/95/07/2026
clause_ref: Para 3(v)
use_when: Insurer stalls Ombudsman proceedings; complainant can request the office to proceed ex parte.

rule_summary: New individual health policies of one year or more have a 30-day free-look period from receipt of the policy document to review and cancel.
verbatim_quote: Every policyholder of life and new individual health insurance policies, except for those policies with tenure of less than a year, shall be provided a free look period of 30 days beginning from the date of receipt of policy document, whether received electronically or otherwise, to review the terms and conditions of such policy.
source_title: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (Protection of Policyholders' Interests, Operations and Allied Matters of Insurers) Regulations, 2024
clause_ref: Regulation 20(1) (Free Look Period of Life and Health Policies)
use_when: Policyholder discovers restrictive terms (sub-limits, room rent caps, co-pay) soon after buying and wants to cancel.
